title: D-DOIT: Training-free Adaptation of Discrete Diffusion via Doob's h-Transform
claim: Reward-unaware sampling can be turned into reward-guided sampling by scoring sampled candidates through a one-pass completion and resampling by reward.
layout: 3 regions: left baseline, right zoom-in steps 1-4, bottom branch; color-coded tokens
description: A three-region diagram using colored token boxes (green A, red T, blue C, yellow G, gray M for masked). The top-left blue panel, 'Standard Discrete Sampling', shows a time axis running from t=L, with all tokens masked, down to t=0, with a clean sequence. Small bar charts sit under the masked positions to show independent per-position reveals. A caption says 'look once → sample once; cheap & blind to reward'. The top-right red panel, 'D-DOIT (one guided reverse step — zoom-in)', lays out four numbered steps. It proposes M=3 candidate sequences, runs a forward pass that completes each into x̂0, scores each with a reward landscape, and draws the next state from a bar chart of h-values. A bottom dashed panel shows optional late-stage best-of-K: one state branches into 4 sequences with reward values, and the highest-reward one is picked. A legend runs along the bottom.
caption: Overview of D-DOIT. Left: Standard masked diffusion unmasks positions independently at each reverse step [ref]; it is cheap but reward-unaware. Right: One guided step approximately tilts the reverse kernel: it draws $M{=}3$ candidates from a tempered proposal [ref], completes and scores them with the prediction head and reward to obtain proxy $h$-values, and selects the next state with sharpened $h$-weights [ref]. Bottom: Optional best-of-$K$ refinement duplicates each trajectory into $K{=}4$ copies after the split and keeps the highest-reward suffix [ref], sharing prefix computation. Revealed tokens stay fixed; the practical sampler does not inherit the exact-target guarantee.
abstract: We propose D-DOIT (Discrete Doob-Oriented Inference-time Transformation), a training-free and efficient adaptation method for discrete diffusion models with generic rewards. D-DOIT formulates adaptation as sampling from a reward-tilted target distribution and realizes this transport through Doob's h-transform of the discrete diffusion reverse kernel, using only reward values rather than reward gradients. Unlike continuous diffusion, masked discrete diffusion samples categorical token-reveal transitions rather than continuous state updates. D-DOIT derives the corresponding discrete Doob's h-transform, which guides sampling by reweighting reverse transition probabilities instead of adding a drift correction. To make this transformation practical, D-DOIT avoids expensive future rollouts. At each guided step, D-DOIT samples candidate next states, uses the model prediction head to complete each candidate into a clean sequence, evaluates each completion with the reward oracle, and resamples the next state with probabilities proportional to the rewards. An optional late-stage best-of-K refinement further improves sample quality by branching trajectories only near the end of denoising, avoiding the $K$-fold cost over the full trajectory. Empirically, across regulatory DNA design and protein inverse folding benchmarks, D-DOIT outperforms training-free guidance baselines. It improves enhancer activity and cell-type specificity while preserving sequence naturalness, and achieves the highest success rate in protein inverse folding.
